report:
The health claim that **soursop (graviola) cures cancer in humans is unsupported by scientific evidence**. 

While preclinical laboratory and animal studies show that bioactive compounds in soursop (*Annona muricata*), particularly acetogenins, can exhibit cytotoxic activity against certain cancer cell lines, these laboratory findings have not been demonstrated in human clinical trials.

Key points regarding the evidence:

* **Lack of Clinical Evidence:** Major medical organizations, including Cancer Research UK and Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, state that there is no clinical evidence or completed human trials proving soursop can treat, prevent, or cure cancer in humans.
* **Safety Risks:** High doses or prolonged consumption of soursop extracts pose health risks. Compounds in soursop (such as annonacin) have neurotoxic properties and have been linked to nerve damage and movement disorders similar to Parkinson's disease.

Medical experts advise against using soursop as an alternative or primary treatment for cancer, as delaying evidence-based medical care can lead to adverse health outcomes.

**Sources:**
* Cancer Research UK: https://www.cancerresearchuk.org/about-cancer/treatment/complementary-alternative-therapies/individual-therapies/graviola
* Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center: https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/graviola
* Verywell Health: https://www.verywellhealth.com/soursop-cancer-5087901
* Outcomes4Me: https://outcomes4me.com/cancer-topic/nutrition/soursop-and-cancer-separating-miracle-claims-from-science/
